title: Climate-driven migration data and governance
bottleneck: Climate displacement is already happening — tens of millions displaced by disasters yearly — yet it is barely measured: no legal category of climate refugee exists, internal displacement goes uncounted in most countries, and slow-onset movement from sea-level rise and desertification is invisible to statistics. Without data and legal frameworks, there is no planned, rights-based response; displacement defaults to crisis and exploitation.
why_it_blocks: Unmanaged climate migration risks humanitarian disasters and political destabilization on a scale that dwarfs current refugee flows. The data and governance vacuum guarantees the response will be reactive, unjust, and inadequate.
current_state: The Platform on Disaster Displacement and some regional frameworks are building norms, and satellite plus mobile data are improving displacement tracking. But binding international protection for climate-displaced people does not exist and is not on the negotiating agenda.
